stark.desc: Grey direwolf on a white field. House of honor and duty.

lannister.desc: Golden lion on a crimson field. The wealthiest of the houses.

targaryen.desc: Red three-headed dragon on a black field. Dynasty of the dragonlords.

baratheon.desc: Black crowned stag on a golden field.

greyjoy.desc: Golden kraken on a black field. A people of seaborne raiders.

martell.desc: Sun and spear. The only house never conquered by the dragons.

tyrell.desc: Golden rose on a green field. A fertile and powerful house.

chars.jon-snow: Bastard of Winterfell, sworn brother of the Night's Watch, later King in the North.
chars.daenerys-targaryen: The Mother of Dragons, exiled heir to the Iron Throne.
chars.tyrion-lannister: A brilliant, cynical Lannister who survives by his wits.
chars.cersei-lannister: A ruthless queen who will do anything to protect her own and her power.
chars.jaime-lannister: The Kingslayer, a knight whose honor is put to the test.
chars.arya-stark: The youngest Stark turned assassin, with a list of names to cross off.
chars.sansa-stark: From court victim to political strategist of the North.
chars.ned-stark: Lord of Winterfell and Hand of the King, rigid about honor.
chars.bran-stark: The Three-Eyed Raven, living memory of the world.
chars.brienne-de-torth: A loyal and fierce knight, true to her word.
chars.theon-greyjoy: A Stark ward torn between two loyalties.
chars.stannis-baratheon: A stubborn claimant to the throne, harsh and exacting.
chars.rhaenyra-targaryen: Designated heir of King Viserys I.
chars.daemon-targaryen: A warrior prince, unpredictable and loyal in his own way.
chars.alicent-hightower: Queen and rival of Rhaenyra, a leading figure of the Greens.
chars.robb-stark: Ned's eldest son, proclaimed King in the North.
chars.catelyn-stark: Ned's wife, a mother who would do anything for her children.
chars.joffrey-baratheon: A cruel and capricious young king.
chars.robert-baratheon: The king of the Iron Throne, victor of the Rebellion.
chars.tywin-lannister: Patriarch of Casterly Rock, obsessed with his house's legacy.
chars.samwell-tarly: A passionate reader and Jon's faithful friend.
chars.davos-mervault: The Onion Knight, Stannis's loyal advisor.
chars.melisandre: Priestess of the Lord of Light.
chars.sandor-clegane: The Hound, a brutal warrior with a quiet code of honor.
chars.jorah-mormont: An exiled knight, Daenerys's faithful advisor.
chars.margaery-tyrell: A shrewd queen who knows how to win over the people.
chars.viserys-targaryen: A peaceful king, torn between his family and the realm.
chars.corlys-velaryon: The Sea Snake, the richest seafarer in Westeros.
chars.bronn: An unscrupulous but funny sellsword who serves whoever pays best. He ends up wealthy in the service of the Lannisters.
chars.varys: The Spider, master of the realm's rumors and spies. He claims to serve the realm before his masters.
chars.jaqen-h-ghar: A Faceless Man of Braavos who can change faces. He initiates Arya into the art of killing.
chars.hodor: A big-hearted stable hand of Winterfell who says only one word. His fate reveals a heartbreaking secret.
chars.ygritte: A red-haired wildling with a strong temper, who teaches Jon Snow that, in her words, "he knows nothing".
chars.tormund-fleau-des-geants: A wildling chief as imposing as he is talkative, whose courage earns him Jon Snow's esteem.
chars.khal-drogo: A powerful Dothraki khal, Daenerys's husband, whose death forces her to forge her own legend.
chars.missandei: A former slave, interpreter and adviser to Daenerys, whose wisdom makes her invaluable.
chars.ver-gris: Commander of the Unsullied, loyal to Daenerys, who finds freedom and love at her side.
chars.podrick-payne: A discreet and devoted squire to Tyrion and then Brienne, whose loyalty grows into true courage.
chars.gilly: A wildling who takes refuge at Castle Black with her son, and becomes close to Samwell.
chars.ramsay-bolton: The cruel bastard of House Bolton, known for his brutality toward his prisoners.
chars.roose-bolton: Icy-calm lord of the Dreadfort, who betrays Robb Stark at the Red Wedding.
chars.walder-frey: Old lord of the Twins, vindictive and prolific, responsible for the Red Wedding massacre.
chars.lysa-arryn: Widow of Jon Arryn and sister of Catelyn, whose paranoia shuts her away in the Eyrie with her son.
chars.olenna-tyrell: The Queen of Thorns, Margaery's grandmother, with a sharp tongue and a formidable mind.
chars.tommen-baratheon: Joffrey's younger brother, a gentle and easily swayed king caught between his mother and the Faith Militant.
chars.euron-greyjoy: Theon's uncle, an exuberant pirate of the Iron Islands who claims to command the greatest fleet in the world.
chars.yara-greyjoy: Balon's daughter and a fearless captain of the Iron Islands, who allies with Daenerys.
chars.roi-de-la-nuit: Leader of the White Walkers and the dead, he leads the army of ice south.
chars.lyanna-mormont: Young lady of Bear Island, who commands respect through her frankness and determination.
chars.barristan-selmy: Former Lord Commander of the Kingsguard, a knight of honor who serves Daenerys in Meereen.
chars.brynden-tully: The Blackfish, Catelyn's uncle and a tenacious defender of Riverrun.
chars.rhaenys-targaryen: The Queen Who Never Was, rider of the dragon Meleys, passed over for the throne by the Great Council.
chars.otto-hightower: An ambitious Hand of the King, Alicent's father, who pushes his daughter toward the throne.
chars.criston-cole: A Kingsguard knight loyal to Alicent and the Greens, whose wounded pride precipitates the war.
chars.aegon-ii-targaryen: Eldest son of Alicent and Viserys, crowned by the Greens and contested by Rhaenyra.
chars.aemond-targaryen: One-eyed prince and rider of the dragon Vhagar, a formidable warrior on the Greens' side.
chars.helaena-targaryen: Sister and wife of Aegon II, anxious and sensitive, whose visions seem to foretell the future.
chars.mysaria: A dancer turned spy in the slums of King's Landing, known as the White Worm.

history.intro: From the dawn of time to the fall of the Iron Throne: five eras tracing the history of Westeros, from the legend of the First Men to the wars that reshaped the realm.

origins.name: The Ancient Times
origins.intro: Before kings and dragons, Westeros belongs to the Children of the Forest and the First Men. The Andals, the Rhoynar and the Doom of Valyria set the stage for the Conquest.

events.t: The Children of the Forest and the First Men
events.d: The First Men cross the Arm of Dorne and cut down the sacred weirwood trees of the Children of the Forest. After centuries of war, the Pact of the Isle of Faces lets the two peoples live side by side.

An endless winter falls upon the world and the White Walkers sweep down from the Far North. The Last Hero drives them back with the help of the Children of the Forest, who, according to the series, had created them to defend themselves.
Brandon the Builder raises the Wall of ice, about 210 meters high and 480 kilometers long, to protect the realm. The Night's Watch has defended it ever since.
Armed with iron and faithful to the Seven, the Andals cross the narrow sea and conquer nearly the whole south of the continent. The North, led by the Stark kings, resists them and keeps the old gods.

events.t: Nymeria and the Rhoynar in Dorne
events.d: Driven from her lands by Valyria, Princess Nymeria leads her Rhoynar ships to Dorne and marries Mors Martell. Dorne has kept its own distinct customs ever since, such as equal inheritance between daughters and sons.
Foreseeing catastrophe, Aenar Targaryen leaves Valyria with his family and his dragons for the island of Dragonstone. This decision will save his house.
About 114 years before the Conquest, a catastrophe destroys the all-powerful Valyria and its dragonlords. The Targaryens are one of the few families to survive.

The continent is divided into rival kingdoms: the North, the Vale, the Iron Islands, the Riverlands, the Westerlands, the Reach, the Stormlands and Dorne. Each has its own kings, wars and shifting alliances.

targaryen.name: The Targaryen Dynasty
targaryen.intro: For nearly three centuries, the dragonlords rule from the Iron Throne. Glory, civil wars and madness mark their dynasty.

events.d: Aegon Targaryen and his sisters Visenya and Rhaenys, riding their dragons, subdue six of the seven kingdoms. The Iron Throne is forged from the swords of the conquered, melted by Balerion's breath.

events.t: Maegor the Cruel and the Red Keep
events.d: Aegon's son, Maegor I, rules through terror and builds Maegor's Holdfast, the core of the Red Keep in King's Landing. His reign remains one of the darkest of the dynasty.
The realm's great lords choose Viserys over his cousin Rhaenys to succeed King Jaehaerys. This precedent will weigh heavily on the next succession.
Under Viserys's peaceful reign, the court splits between his daughter Rhaenyra, named heir, and the new queen Alicent Hightower. These rivalries foreshadow war.

events.t: The Dance of the Dragons (129–131 AC)
events.d: When Viserys dies, Rhaenyra and her half-brother Aegon II fight over the throne: the civil war of the Blacks against the Greens, told in House of the Dragon. Many dragons perish.
After the Dance, the dragons die one after another, for lack of care and viable clutches. The last dies around 153 AC, and Targaryen magic wanes.

events.t: Dunk & Egg and the Blackfyre Rebellion (around 196 AC)
events.d: Daemon Blackfyre, the king's bastard son, rebels against his half-brother, King Daeron II, and loses the battle of the Redgrass Field. In those days, the hedge knight Dunk and his squire Egg roam the roads.

events.t: Aerys II, the Mad King (262–283 AC)
events.d: Aerys II sinks little by little into paranoia and cruelty, fascinated by wildfire. His reign leads to the revolt of the realm's greatest lords.

rebellion.name: Robert's Rebellion
rebellion.intro: A tournament, an abduction and a king too paranoid: Robert Baratheon's rebellion ends the Targaryen dynasty and upends the balance among the great houses.

events.d: Prince Rhaegar Targaryen crowns Lyanna Stark queen of love and beauty, much to the dismay of her betrothed, Robert Baratheon. This episode is remembered by all as the spark of the conflict.
Lyanna is abducted by Rhaegar, according to the official version. Her father Rickard and her brother Brandon come to King's Landing to demand justice: King Aerys has them both executed.
Eddard Stark, Robert Baratheon and Jon Arryn refuse to obey Aerys, who demands their heads, and call their bannermen. The Tullys soon join the rebels.
At the ford of the Trident, Robert Baratheon faces Prince Rhaegar, heir of the Targaryens, and kills him in single combat. This victory opens the road to King's Landing for the rebels.
Tywin Lannister brings his troops into the capital, officially to defend the king. Jaime Lannister kills Aerys to stop him from burning the city, and Rhaegar's children are slaughtered.
Robert Baratheon takes the Iron Throne and marries Cersei Lannister to seal the alliance with the wealthy House of Casterly Rock. Ned Stark returns to Winterfell.

events.t: The exile of Viserys and Daenerys
events.d: The last living Targaryens, the children Viserys and Daenerys, flee to Essos and live from exile to exile. Daenerys was born on Dragonstone during the storm that ravaged the island.

Balon Greyjoy, king of the Iron Islands, tries to win back his independence. Crushed by Robert, the rebellion costs the lives of his eldest sons and means that Theon, his youngest, grows up as a hostage of the Starks.

five-kings.name: The War of the Five Kings
five-kings.intro: A king's death sets off the greatest conflict Westeros has known in centuries: five claimants clash amid intrigue, betrayal and battle.

events.t: Ned Stark becomes Hand of the King
events.d: When Jon Arryn dies, Robert asks his old friend Ned to become his Hand. In King's Landing, Ned uncovers the secrets of the court, notably the truth about the queen's children.

events.t: The death of Robert and the execution of Ned
events.d: The king dies after a hunting accident, and Joffrey takes the throne. Ned is arrested for treason and beheaded, plunging the Starks into war.
Joffrey, Robb Stark, Renly and Stannis Baratheon, then Balon Greyjoy all proclaim themselves king. The realm tears itself apart through alliances, betrayals and battles.
Stannis besieges King's Landing by sea, but Tyrion Lannister sets the river ablaze with wildfire. The arrival of Tywin and the Tyrells saves the city.
At a wedding hosted by Walder Frey, Robb Stark, his mother Catelyn and much of his army are slaughtered. This episode is one of the most famous of the whole saga.

events.t: Joffrey's wedding and the death of Tywin
events.d: Joffrey is poisoned at his own wedding, and Tyrion is accused of the crime. Tyrion escapes and kills his father Tywin, leaving House Lannister without a real leader.
Daenerys, now mother of three dragons, frees the slaves of Astapor, Yunkai and Meereen. She learns to rule, but also, at her own expense, the limits of power.
Mance Rayder gathers the wildlings north of the Wall, fleeing the White Walkers. Jon Snow and the Night's Watch defend Castle Black in a decisive battle.

long-night.name: The Long Night and Beyond
long-night.period: After the War of the Five Kings
long-night.intro: While the houses tear each other apart, the true threat marches south. The war against the dead, then the struggle for the Iron Throne, seal the fate of Westeros.

events.d: Elected Lord Commander of the Night's Watch, Jon opens the Wall to the wildlings. His brothers stab him for treason, but Melisandre brings him back to life.
Jon and Sansa retake Winterfell from Ramsay Bolton in a terrible clash. Jon is proclaimed King in the North by the region's lords.
To escape her trial, Cersei blows up the Great Sept of Baelor with wildfire, killing her enemies. King Tommen takes his own life, and Cersei has herself crowned queen.
Daenerys lands on Dragonstone with her dragons, her army and her allies. There she meets Jon, with whom she allies against the threat from the North.
The living face the Night King's army of the dead. Arya Stark kills the Night King and ends the Long Night.
Daenerys, driven to the brink of madness by her losses, burns King's Landing with her dragon despite the city's surrender. The city is reduced to ashes.
Jon Snow, torn, stabs Daenerys, and the dragon Drogon carries off her body. Tyrion and the lords of Westeros gather to decide the future of the realm.

events.t: Bran the Broken and the independent North
events.d: Bran Stark is chosen to rule the Six Kingdoms, while the North becomes independent under Queen Sansa. Jon returns to the Night's Watch, then goes beyond the Wall.

places.name: Winterfell
places.desc: Seat of House Stark for thousands of years, the fortress is built over hot springs. It is also the setting of the battle against the dead.

places.name: The Wall
places.desc: A wall of ice roughly 210 meters high that separates the Seven Kingdoms from the wild lands of the Far North. The Night's Watch has defended it for centuries.

places.name: Castle Black
places.desc: Main fortress of the Night's Watch, at the foot of the Wall. It is where Jon Snow takes his vows, then becomes Lord Commander.

places.name: The Dreadfort
places.desc: Stronghold of House Bolton, known for the cruelty of its lords and their flayed men. Theon Greyjoy is held prisoner there.

places.name: King's Landing
places.desc: Capital of the Seven Kingdoms, home to the Red Keep and the Iron Throne. It is the center of all the intrigues of the court.

places.name: Dragonstone
places.desc: Volcanic island where the Targaryens settled before the Conquest. Daenerys returns there with her dragons to reclaim her kingdom.

places.name: Casterly Rock
places.desc: Fortress carved into a cliff, seat of House Lannister, famed for its gold mines.

places.name: Riverrun
places.desc: Castle of the Tullys, at the meeting of two rivers, whose natural defenses make it hard to besiege.

places.name: The Twins
places.desc: Two towers linked by a bridge that controls the crossing of the Trident. The seat of Walder Frey, it is the scene of the Red Wedding.

places.name: Harrenhal
places.desc: A gigantic ruined fortress, once the largest in Westeros, whose towers, scorched by dragons, are said to be cursed.

places.name: The Eyrie
places.desc: Fortress of the Arryns perched on a mountainside, reputed to be impregnable. Prisoners are thrown out through the Moon Door.

places.name: Highgarden
places.desc: Castle of House Tyrell, surrounded by gardens and fertile land that feed much of the realm.

places.name: Oldtown
places.desc: The oldest city in Westeros, home to the Citadel where maesters are trained, and to House Hightower.

places.name: Storm's End
places.desc: Castle of the Baratheons, said to have been built to withstand the storms of the sea. Stannis is besieged there during the rebellion.

places.name: Sunspear
places.desc: Capital of Dorne and seat of House Martell, where succession customs differ from the rest of the realm.

places.name: Pyke
places.desc: Sea-battered island ruled by House Greyjoy. Its people, skilled sailors, live by plunder and raiding.

places.name: Valyria
places.desc: City-state of the dragonlords, destroyed by the Doom. Its ruins and its Valyrian steel feed every legend.

places.name: Braavos
places.desc: Free city built on islands, with its colossal Titan and its Iron Bank. Arya joins the House of Black and White there.

places.name: Meereen
places.desc: City of Slaver's Bay where Daenerys abolishes slavery and takes her first steps as a queen.

places.name: Qarth
places.desc: Merchant city with legendary walls, where Daenerys looks for allies and finds the House of the Undying.

places.name: Vaes Dothrak
places.desc: Sacred city of the Dothraki, without walls, where all the widows of khals come to live among the dosh khaleen.

battles.name: The Field of Fire
battles.desc: Aegon and his sisters attack the armies of the Reach and the Westerlands on dragonback. Thousands of men perish in the flames, and the kings bend the knee.

battles.name: The Redgrass Field
battles.desc: Decisive battle of the first Blackfyre Rebellion, in which the rebel bastard is defeated. It leaves a lasting mark on the Targaryen dynasty.

battles.name: The Trident
battles.desc: Robert Baratheon kills Prince Rhaegar in single combat, opening the road to King's Landing for the rebels.

battles.name: The Sack of King's Landing
battles.desc: Tywin's troops enter the capital and sack it. Jaime kills King Aerys, known as the Mad King.

battles.name: The Whispering Wood
battles.desc: Robb's first great victory, in which he traps Jaime Lannister's army despite being outnumbered.

battles.name: The Blackwater
battles.desc: Stannis attacks King's Landing by sea, but Tyrion sets the river ablaze with wildfire. The arrival of Tywin and the Tyrells saves the city.

battles.name: The Red Wedding
battles.desc: More than a battle, a massacre: Robb, Catelyn and their bannermen are murdered during a wedding feast.

battles.name: Castle Black
battles.desc: Jon Snow and the Night's Watch hold out against Mance Rayder's army as it tries to cross the Wall.

battles.name: Meereen
battles.desc: Daenerys returns on her dragon Drogon and destroys the fleet of the Masters, who came with their allies to besiege the city.

battles.name: The Battle of the Bastards
battles.sides: Jon and Sansa vs. Ramsay Bolton
battles.desc: Before the walls of Winterfell, Jon is about to be crushed until the knights of the Vale turn the tide. House Stark takes back its home.

battles.name: The Sack of the Reach
battles.desc: Daenerys and Drogon attack the Lannister supply convoy, showing for the first time the power of a dragon at war.

battles.name: The Battle of Winterfell
battles.desc: The armies of Westeros face the Night King. Arya's victory ends the threat of the White Walkers.

battles.name: The Fall of King's Landing
battles.desc: Daenerys destroys Cersei's fleet, then the city itself, despite the ringing of the surrender bell. The capital is reduced to ashes.

battles.name: The Dance of the Dragons
battles.desc: Civil war between the supporters of Rhaenyra and those of Aegon II, in which dragons also clash. It decimates the Targaryens.

beliefs.name: The Faith of the Seven
beliefs.desc: The main religion of southern Westeros: a single deity with seven faces (the Father, the Mother, the Maiden, the Warrior, the Smith, the Crone and the Stranger). Its septons and septs shape life at court.

beliefs.name: The Old Gods
beliefs.desc: Worship of the First Men and the Children of the Forest, offered to the weirwood trees with carved faces. The Starks and the wildlings remain faithful to it.

beliefs.name: The Lord of Light
beliefs.desc: A fire god from Essos, worshipped by red priests like Melisandre, who believe in an eternal war between light and darkness.

beliefs.name: The Drowned God
beliefs.desc: Deity of the Iron Islands, revered by the Greyjoys. His faithful practice baptism by drowning, from which they return consecrated.

beliefs.name: The Many-Faced God
beliefs.desc: God of death in Braavos, served by the Faceless Men. His motto, "Valar Morghulis", is a reminder that all men must die.

beliefs.name: The Great Stallion
beliefs.desc: God of the Dothraki, represented by a gigantic horse. The khals are bound to him, and the nomadic peoples believe in him.

beliefs.name: The Faith Militant
beliefs.desc: Armed movement of the Faith of the Seven, restored by Cersei Lannister. The Sparrows impose their own justice in King's Landing under the leadership of the High Sparrow.

creatures.name: Dragons
creatures.desc: Beasts of fire that allowed the Targaryens to conquer Westeros. Extinct for a century, they are reborn thanks to Daenerys, who raises Drogon, Rhaegal and Viserion.

creatures.name: Direwolves
creatures.desc: Giant wolves, emblem of the Starks. Each Stark child receives one at Winterfell, like Ghost for Jon or Nymeria for Arya.

creatures.name: The White Walkers
creatures.desc: Creatures of ice from the Far North, able to raise the dead. In the series, their leader is the Night King.

creatures.name: Wights
creatures.desc: Corpses raised by the White Walkers that form the army of the dead. Only fire, obsidian and Valyrian steel can destroy them.

creatures.name: Giants and Mammoths
creatures.desc: A people of enormous size living beyond the Wall. They are allies of the wildlings and fight alongside their mammoths.

creatures.name: The Children of the Forest
creatures.desc: An ancient, small people, the first inhabitants of Westeros, masters of a magic tied to the weirwood trees.

creatures.name: The Three-Eyed Raven
creatures.desc: Mystical being whose memory spans the entire past. Bran becomes his successor after traveling beyond the Wall.

creatures.name: Messenger Ravens
creatures.desc: Birds trained by the maesters to carry letters between castles, often heralds of grave news.

got.d: Ned Stark becomes Hand of the King and uncovers a secret that threatens the throne. On the other side of the world, Daenerys marries a Dothraki lord.
The War of the Five Kings breaks out: Robb Stark, Stannis, Renly and Balon Greyjoy stand against Joffrey. The Blackwater closes the season.
The Lannisters gain the upper hand while Daenerys frees the Unsullied. The Red Wedding upends the war.
Joffrey's wedding ends in tragedy and Tyrion is put on trial. In the North, the Night's Watch prepares for the wildling assault.
Cersei leans on the Faith Militant before becoming its victim, and Jon is elected Lord Commander. Daenerys struggles to govern Meereen.
Jon returns to life and House Stark retakes Winterfell. Cersei blows up the Great Sept.
Daenerys lands in Westeros and allies with Jon. The armies of the living prepare to face the dead.
The Battle of Winterfell ends the Long Night, then the struggle for the Iron Throne comes to a close in King's Landing.

hotd.d: King Viserys names Rhaenyra as his heir, but the court is divided over his succession. Tensions between his daughter and Queen Alicent grow over the years.
Civil war breaks out between the Blacks and the Greens. Dragons become the decisive weapon of the conflict.
The Dance of the Dragons continues, with alliances forming and falling apart. A fourth and final season is announced for 2028.

aknight.d: Ser Duncan the Tall, a hedge knight, takes young Egg as his squire and crosses Westeros, far from the great intrigues. A season 2 is expected in 2027.
